items.item: The boxed-vs-packed ratio (about four and a half times on a representative run) is measured directly on this sandbox's own CPython via sys.getsizeof, deduplicated by object id to avoid double-counting CPython's own small-int cache, not taken from a textbook figure

at.step: Reveal: the lab — boxed vs. packed, measured for real

items.item: The __slots__ measurement confirms directly (via hasattr) that the slotted instance has no __dict__ attribute at all, not merely a smaller one, which is the actual mechanism behind the memory saving rather than just its side effect

at.step: Reveal: the lab — __slots__, measured for real

items.item: The specializing interpreter's real effect is shown by disassembling the identical function before any call and after warm-up with two different argument types, rather than asserting PEP 659's claim secondhand

at.step: Reveal: the lab — the interpreter disassembled, cold and then warm

items.item: This sandbox's CPython build is checked directly for the experimental JIT (sys._jit absent) and free-threading (Py_GIL_DISABLED is 0) rather than assumed from the version number, so every claim about either feature's own effect is disclosed as sourced-only rather than locally measured
